name: Economics and Science for Environmental Sustainability
overview: The degree joins economics, management and natural science around one question: how societies can run on a sustainable footing. You take core courses in management, marketing, microeconomics and mathematics, then move into energy economics, market failures and regulation, and international environmental law. The science side covers biological resources, ecosystems and technosystems, and Earth systems and climate change, so you learn to read environmental problems from both an economic and a scientific angle. It is built for work on climate change and corporate responsibility.

name: Physical Sciences for Innovative Technologies
overview: You build a solid grounding in physics and then apply it to areas where technology is changing quickly: solutions for the green-energy transition, quantum technologies and digital innovation. Data analysis and laboratory techniques run through the course, so you gain practical experimental skills alongside theory. Teaching mixes on-campus sessions with online activity such as virtual study groups, forums and personal feedback from instructors. The degree is run jointly with the University of Pavia, with teaching based in Milan and Pavia, and it prepares you for research and technology-driven industry.

name: Economics
overview: You learn economic theory, micro and macro, on a base of mathematics, statistics, econometrics and machine learning, then use those tools on real questions such as crime, health, climate and economic outcomes. Teaching relies on group work, business cases, discussion and testimonials from practitioners, and a coding course trains you to solve problems with data. From the second semester of year two you choose between Economic Sciences, which leans on mathematical modelling and cognitive science, and Economic and Data Sciences, which centres on algorithms and machine learning. Graduates go into economic or management consulting, finance, public and non-governmental institutions and research, or on to quantitative master's programmes.

name: Finance
overview: The degree explains how the financial system fits together, from capital markets and financial intermediaries to contracts and instruments, and it trains you to measure risk with quantitative methods. Typical coursework in a finance bachelor of this kind covers accounting, corporate finance, asset pricing, economics, statistics and mathematics, and the page stresses a data-driven approach to financial decisions. Classes use business cases, group projects and a coding course, and the programme offers international exchange options. Graduates move into financial careers with the help of the university's employer links, or continue to a master's in finance.

name: International Politics and Government
overview: The degree teaches political science through politics, economics, management, law, history and quantitative methods, following policy through three phases: designing it, putting it into practice and evaluating it with modern techniques. You look at how national and international institutions decide and how private actors deal with the public sector. Teaching is active, with group work, business cases and a coding course. The Politics and Policy Making track includes a compulsory semester at a partner university and an optional internship. Graduates work in public institutions, NGOs, consultancy and lobbying firms, and multinationals in regulated sectors.

name: International Politics and Government, HEC-Bocconi double degree
overview: You split six semesters evenly between Milan and HEC Paris. The first year in Milan covers economics, comparative public law, politics and the public sector, quantitative methods for the social sciences, and coding and data visualisation in Python. Year two is shared: governance of digital technologies, social media and democracy and a deep learning module in Milan, then business analytics, European governance and behavioural and cognitive science at HEC. The final year in Paris adds climate change and sustainability, research methods, field work, a capstone project and a final paper. The mix prepares you for roles where data science meets the social sciences.

name: Management
overview: You study how companies work as a whole, looking at business functions such as logistics, marketing and finance, at different kinds of organisation including commercial firms, manufacturers and public administration, and at the economic setting around them. The aim is an integrated view of the firm and a set of analytical tools you can use as conditions change. Classes lean on business cases, guest speakers and group work, and a coding course trains you to tackle complex problems. Typical first-year subjects in a management bachelor include accounting, economics, mathematics and statistics. International exchange options are available, and career staff link graduates to a large network of employers.

name: Management and Computer Science
overview: The degree combines mathematics, statistics, computing and machine learning with economics and the legal side of data, so that you can collect, organise, analyse and interpret data for business and financial decisions. It is aimed at future managers who want a full picture of the world of data rather than a purely technical role. Teaching uses the latest technology, close contact with instructors, group work, business cases, talks by practitioners and discussion, and a coding course builds problem-solving skills. International mobility is offered, and career services help graduates reach employers.

name: Management for the Arts and Cultures
overview: You learn management and economics alongside arts and humanities, studying artistic, cultural and creative practice together with the institutional, economic and legal frameworks around it. The sectors covered include museums, heritage and art markets, theatre and performing arts, publishing, music, film, media, fashion, design, communication and urban development. Learning is project-based and multidisciplinary, with group work, business cases, discussion and a coding course. The degree prepares you for roles in cultural organisations and the creative industries, where technology and cultural diversity keep changing the work.

name: Mathematical and Computing Sciences for Artificial Intelligence
overview: The degree rests on three pillars: mathematical tools (analysis, geometry, probability, statistics and numerical calculation), modelling through physics, including quantum physics, and economics such as game theory, and computation through theoretical computer science, algorithms and programming. Machine learning and computational statistics sit on top of that base, with an emphasis on rigorous theory as well as application. Teaching includes group work, business cases, talks by practitioners and discussion. Graduates can continue to a master's in AI, applied mathematics, computer science, data science, physics, economics or finance, or work as methodological experts in mathematics, modelling and AI.

name: World Bachelor in Business
overview: A solid grounding in business and economics is paired with liberal arts courses in writing, science and the humanities, and each year carries a regional theme: technology and entertainment in Los Angeles, global banking and financial leadership in Hong Kong, and European integration in Milan. In the final year you pick any of the three partner schools to specialise. Internships are arranged in each country, and extracurricular activities introduce local business language and culture, so cultural immersion is part of the course. You finish with three bachelor's degrees, one from each partner, and graduates are well placed for jobs in international businesses and organisations.

name: Bachelor in Global Law
overview: You learn the theory and practice of law alongside business management, finance, economics and digital technology, with attention to the global side of legal questions: how institutions work, how individual rights are protected and how organisations, for-profit and non-profit, stay compliant. Learning is active, through group work, legal clinics and moot court competitions, plus seminars on negotiation, advocacy, legal writing and public speaking. A required law-in-action experience means either an internship or pro-bono clinic work, and in the third year you shape your own path. Graduates work as junior legal profiles in consultancy, regulation and paralegal roles, or continue to a JD, LLM or master's.

name: Business Administration and Management
overview: You learn business economics, accounting, marketing and law, then look at how organisations take decisions, handle finance and banking, read balance sheets and use budgeting and planning tools. The course is practice-oriented, with project work, real business cases, design thinking, role plays and guest speakers from industry, and you work with companies from the first year. Sustainability, tourism, food and beverage and culture feature as sectors. Exchange and internships abroad are possible, and a double degree with Toulouse School of Management is on offer. Graduates go into management and consulting, sales, banking, finance, public administration, human resources and marketing.

name: Digital Management
overview: The degree covers four linked areas: economics and digital law, digital technology such as IT systems, networks and big data, organisation and strategy for innovation with AI, blockchain and Industry 4.0, and marketing and communication built on data and e-commerce. Classes are held with the H-FARM College, which brings entrepreneurship into the academic work. You learn through projects, lab work, workshops with business leaders, networking events, business challenges and guest sessions, with internship support from the career service. Graduates work as digital managers, business analysts, innovation or project managers, data analysts, marketing and e-commerce specialists, or found their own start-ups.

name: Economics and Business
overview: The degree blends economics, law, quantitative analysis and business management, with attention to financial systems and markets and to global economic challenges. Teaching builds specialist and soft skills together, and you can study or intern abroad through Erasmus+ and overseas exchanges, or do a training internship in Italy through the career service. Graduates go into companies, public institutions and international organisations, working for instance as economic or financial consultants, market analysts and financial specialists in banking, or they continue to postgraduate study.

name: Computer Science (Data Science curriculum)
overview: You learn to design, build and manage systems that generate, transmit and process information, together with statistical methods for analysing data. The English-taught Data Science curriculum focuses on data analysis using statistics and artificial intelligence, alongside two other curricula, one in Italian on software development and a European one with a year abroad and a double degree. Teaching combines theory with laboratory work and company internships, and also covers the legal and ethical side of the profession. Graduates work in software development, data analysis and IT administration in companies, public bodies and research labs, or continue to the English-taught master's in Computer Science and Information Technology.

name: Hospitality Innovation and e-Tourism
overview: The degree combines three strands: management skills such as finance, human resources, organisation and industry regulation, digital tools such as property management systems, CRM, social media strategy and data analytics, and cultural and territorial knowledge including museology, history and geography. Learning is hands-on, with workshops, labs and three internships, one each year, that move from operational to supervisory roles, with partners such as the Fondazione Scuola Italiana di Ospitalita and TH Resorts. Graduates work as middle managers in hotels, destination management and tourism firms, or in digital marketing and online travel agencies, and some go on to a master's in hospitality or tourism.

name: Ancient Civilizations for the Contemporary World
overview: You study ancient societies across the Mediterranean, the Middle East and Asia, combining social and anthropological analysis, work with source texts, and language and philology, with an eye on how cultures connect and differ. Classes run in a blended format between the Venice and Milan campuses, in person with live streaming and tutors supporting the remote classrooms, as the degree is shared with the University of Milan. Graduates look to museums, archaeological sites and exhibitions, cultural communication, and consulting for the entertainment industry on historical themes, while guiding tourists requires extra postgraduate training.

name: Italian and Mediterranean Studies
overview: A single curriculum joins language, literature, history, the arts and geopolitics to look at Italy's place in the Mediterranean from ancient to contemporary times, through texts, documents, artworks and social practices. Subjects include Mediterranean history, comparative literature, archaeology and art, intercultural communication and digital scholarship, with optional modules to shape your own path. You can apply what you learn through activities and internships, or study abroad on Erasmus+ and overseas exchanges. Graduates go into museums, cultural organisations, publishing, tourism and international projects, education, content creation and Euro-Mediterranean cooperation.

name: Philosophy, International and Economic Studies
overview: Modelled on the Oxford PPE idea, the degree joins philosophy with economics, politics, history and law, pairing a logical and philosophical approach with the social and economic sciences to make sense of global, political and cultural questions. You read demanding texts, learn to put forward solutions to current problems, and attend a public lecture series with visiting scholars. Exchange semesters abroad and internships are available, and a double degree exists with University College Groningen. Graduates work in analysis and consulting, public relations and policy roles in agencies and international bodies, or continue to master's programmes such as Economics and Finance or Comparative International Relations.

name: Business and Finance
overview: The degree pairs core business and finance with newer fields: data science and analytics and the use of artificial intelligence in business. Typical courses in a degree of this kind include accounting, corporate finance, economics, marketing, law, mathematics and statistics, with a multidisciplinary approach throughout. Theory is tied to practice through links with local companies in Brescia and the wider business community, and the focus is on small and medium-sized firms. Graduates are prepared for careers in both local and international business settings.

name: Communication Management
overview: You study communication through sociology, psychology, political science, economics and media studies, with specialised focus on fashion, food and lifestyle. Labs and workshops put you on real projects with professors and industry professionals, building skills in integrated campaign design, social media content, event planning and communication analytics. Being in Milan gives you access to creative networks in fashion, design, media and food. Graduates are prepared for work in media and public relations, brand strategy, campaign management and communication analysis.

name: Criminology
overview: The degree draws on sociology, psychology and political science and adds criminal law and justice systems, crime prevention strategies, security studies and the use of technology and data analysis in crime research. You compare how criminal justice works in different countries and learn the methods used to examine crime trends. The programme works with Transcrime, a research centre that provides current insights and practical tools for crime analysis, and being in Milan connects you to European crime prevention networks and policy institutions. It is described as the only English-taught undergraduate criminology degree in continental Europe.

name: Economics and Management
overview: Four strands run through the degree: economics and finance, management and business strategy, law and political economy, and mathematics, statistics and data tools. Courses connect economic and management theory with real business situations, using applied project work, and the programme builds in internships and international exchange options. Milan's position as a financial centre gives contact with multinationals, banks, consultancies and start-ups. The aim is to train analysts and decision-makers for competitive global job markets.

name: Finance
overview: You cover business and political economics, corporate finance and financial markets, law and regulation, and quantitative methods and data analysis. Alongside lectures, learning relies on projects, group work, simulations and role play led by finance professionals, with soft-skills and digital training and specialist lectures on emerging financial topics. The curriculum draws on partnerships with leaders and practitioners in the finance industry. Studying in Milan, home to the Italian Stock Exchange, multinational banks and asset managers, ties the course closely to financial practice and career development.

name: Food Production Management
overview: The degree combines agricultural science and food technology, agri-food business and value chain management, sustainability and environmental impact, and food safety, quality and regulation, with a focus on Italian food systems such as dairy, meat, cereals and horticulture. You learn processing and preservation, quality control, certification, regulatory compliance and supply chain economics. Teaching is hands-on, with a sensory lab, case studies that follow the whole food chain from farm to table and applied training from farming to business strategy. Piacenza lies in Emilia-Romagna's food-producing region. Graduates are prepared for roles in sustainability, quality assurance, compliance and economic strategy in the food industry.

name: International Business Management
overview: You study business, economics, law and data analysis while building teamwork, digital innovation and leadership skills, and you can specialise through a Vertical track that focuses on a chosen industry. Learning is applied: business labs, group projects, real-world projects and a mandatory internship, with optional exchange periods abroad. A selective double-degree route has you spend the first two years in Piacenza and two more at a partner university in France, Germany, Spain, the USA or Mexico, ending with two qualifications. The aim is work in international companies and global careers.

name: International Relations and Global Affairs
overview: The degree is interdisciplinary: political science and international relations, history and regional studies, international economics and economic geography, international law and global institutions, and sociology and social psychology. Core topics are diplomacy, conflict resolution, international development and global governance. Classes are small, with seminars and guest lectures from international scholars and practitioners, and you work on practical projects with international institutions and organisations. Milan is a European centre for diplomacy, media and NGOs, which helps with networking. Graduates look to diplomacy, policy analysis, development work and international cooperation.

name: Psychology
overview: The curriculum is organised around four areas: mind and development through cognitive and developmental psychology, brain and behaviour through neuroscience, health and society through clinical and social psychology, and evidence and methods through quantitative research and data analysis. Teaching follows an active learning model of lectures, lab work and seminars with specialised teaching assistants, in small classes with close tutoring. Students who want a research route can join an honours track. The degree combines traditional and modern topics within a multidisciplinary framework, drawing on more than a century of psychology teaching and research at the university.

name: Medicine and Surgery (Rome)
overview: Over six years taught in English, you move from the basic sciences towards clinical medicine; typical early courses in such a degree include anatomy, physiology and biochemistry. From the early years you train inside Rome's Gemelli Hospital, observing doctors, learning clinical procedures and taking part in hospital life. The course adds ethics, medical anthropology, law and doctor-patient communication to the science, and its structure is aligned with international standards, including preparation for USMLE Step 1 and Step 2. Graduates are prepared to practise as independent doctors in Italy and in other countries such as the US and UK.

name: Medicine and Surgery (Bolzano)
overview: Over six years you work through the basic medical sciences and then clinical medicine, with ethics, patient communication and healthcare law woven in. Lectures are in English, while clinical internships run in German and Italian, reflecting the bilingual healthcare system of South Tyrol, and teaching is shared between Bolzano and Rome's Gemelli Hospital. The course combines European medical education with training aligned to US systems. Graduates are prepared to work as doctors in multilingual and cross-border healthcare settings across Europe, especially in Italian and German-speaking countries.

name: Business Administration
overview: The first two years build the base: microeconomics, accounting, calculus, corporate law, management theory, statistics and macroeconomics, then marketing, financial analysis, EU law and corporate finance, with coding labs and specialised software training. Learning is project-based, including a Grand Challenge practical component and an internship or company project. In the third year you choose a major in Marketing, Organizational Behavior and HR, or International Business and Strategy. International options include the ACE triple degree with Renmin University and George Washington University, Erasmus+ and free-mover semesters. Graduates go into multinationals, start-ups, consulting, financial institutions and marketing management.

name: Economics and Business
overview: A shared two-year foundation covers micro and macroeconomics, international economics, mathematics, statistics and applied econometrics, business economics, accounting, corporate finance, law, and data analysis and coding. In the third year you pick a major: Management, Finance, or Economics, which looks at growth, development, inequality, public policy and competition. Teaching mixes lectures, workshops, project work, simulations and real-world cases. Exchange options include the EU-TriBE triple degree with Universite libre de Bruxelles and Goethe University Frankfurt, Erasmus+ and free-mover semesters. Graduates go into consulting, finance, strategy and international organisations, or on to a master's.

name: Global Law
overview: Years one and two give every student a shared grounding in constitutional, private, EU, administrative, international, comparative and criminal law. In year three you choose Global Law, Business and Tech, which looks at law and technology and financial markets, Global Law and International Organizations, or an Italian Law track with a fast route to a single-cycle master's. Teaching goes beyond lectures to workshops, project work, simulations, legal clinics and the Grand Challenge. Exchanges and summer schools are available. Graduates work in European and international institutions, NGOs and multinationals, in compliance and institutional relations, or go on to a master's in law or international relations.

name: Management and Artificial Intelligence
overview: Year one covers mathematics, programming, microeconomics, algorithms, digital business management and statistical modelling, with labs on real challenges from industry or academia. Year two moves to machine learning, organisational data integration and social network analysis, anchored by the Grand Challenge, where groups apply data analysis and AI to real business problems. In year three you study databases, financial technologies and AI regulation, with electives, an internship and a final thesis. No prior IT knowledge is needed. A double degree exists with Kozminski University. Graduates work in data analysis, AI strategy and digital transformation, or continue to master's programmes in data science and AI.

name: Politics: Philosophy and Economics
overview: The first year covers microeconomics, contemporary history, sociology, political philosophy, public law, statistics and mathematical analysis, plus an AI literacy and coding lab; the second adds macroeconomics, international relations, political science, the history of political thought, social research methods and EU and international law. In year three you pick a concentration in Artificial Intelligence, Sustainability or Fundamental Rights. Teaching includes data analysis workshops, seminars, internships and study abroad, with double degrees with Victoria University of Wellington and Sciences Po Bordeaux. Graduates move into international organisations, government, think tanks, NGOs and companies, or on to a master's.

name: Architectural Design (English track)
overview: You study design and architectural composition alongside history and theory, conservation of historic buildings, building physics, structural mechanics, materials and construction technology, with mathematics for representation, urban design, sociology and project evaluation. Design training is central: multidisciplinary studios work hand in hand with theory courses, supported by seminars, workshops and study trips, and a mandatory internship links you to professional practice. Graduates work in design firms, public institutions and construction management, and can register as junior architects after the state exam or continue to a master's in architecture, landscape or urban planning.

name: Civil Engineering (English track)
overview: The first year is mathematics, physics, chemistry and computer science. The second brings the core civil subjects: structural mechanics and design, geotechnics, fluid mechanics, hydraulic engineering, infrastructure and transport design, and surveying and monitoring. In the third year you apply them to steel and reinforced concrete design, earthworks, hydraulic projects and transport infrastructure, with material technology and construction management alongside. Graduates work in the public or private sector on soils, structures, transport, hydraulics, civil protection and surveying, and can sit the professional exam as junior engineers or continue to a master's in Civil Engineering, Risk Mitigation or Built Environment Management.

name: Engineering Science
overview: The degree has four parts. A core area in the first two years blends mathematics, physics, chemistry, materials and computer science, with Engineering Corners that introduce methods from across engineering. In years two and three, a direction area of electives points you toward fields such as mechanics, fluids, automation or electronics, and a third-year focus area goes deeper into one. It ends with a hands-on interdisciplinary capstone project, often with industry or research labs. Teaching mixes lectures, hands-on and virtual labs, group projects and presentations. Graduates work where engineering fields meet, or continue to specialised master's degrees.

name: Industrial Engineering
overview: You study mechanical systems and manufacturing technologies, industrial automation, operations and logistics, data analysis and decision-making, and sustainability and energy management, across three terms each year. Lectures are matched with integrated lab sessions, team projects, case studies from partner companies and simulation software, with daily class time kept to four or five hours to leave room for independent work. In the last term of year three you choose between a company internship tied to your thesis or a project with industry or research teams. Graduates work in manufacturing, automation, logistics, operations and quality, or continue to master's degrees in Mechanical, Energy, Management or Automation and Control Engineering.

name: Process Engineering
overview: After a first stage in mathematics, physics, chemistry and computer science, you move into automation and control, materials, production systems management and information engineering, then model identification, data analysis, digital twins and process simulation, with sustainable and circular engineering throughout. Teaching mixes lectures, labs, group projects and work with industrial partners, and electives tailor the final year. A capstone project, which can be an internship, project work or a collaboration with industry or research, completes the degree. Graduates work in production, process design, automation and quality in chemical, pharmaceutical, energy and food firms, or go on to a master's.

name: Interaction Design
overview: You learn the full design process for products, services and interactive systems that mix digital and physical parts, starting from user needs, how people interact, usability and accessibility. The curriculum draws on design, humanities, technology and representation, with a focus on interactive artefacts, digital interfaces and IoT systems. Lectures are combined with design studios and workshops, where you practise programming, prototyping and representation by doing. The degree is taught in English on the Lecco campus. Graduates work as interaction designers, UX and UI designers or information architects in design studios, technology companies and agencies, or continue to Politecnico's master's in Digital and Interaction Design.

name: Architecture (English-taught)
overview: The degree centres on architectural design and planning at several scales: you learn to design simple civic buildings, survey modern and historic buildings and work through a project from first concept to management. Typical courses in a degree of this kind include design studios, history of architecture, drawing and representation, structures and building technology, and mathematics. Learning happens in design studios, labs and projects, workshops, an internship and a thesis. Graduates work as junior architects in design studios, public administration, engineering and architecture firms and construction companies, and can continue to a master's.

name: Automotive Engineering (entirely in English)
overview: The course treats the motor vehicle as an integrated system and trains junior designers to contribute to developing and producing it. After the usual engineering foundation in mathematics, physics and computing, typical courses in this field cover vehicle sub-systems, mechanical design, materials, powertrain and production processes. Learning is practical and team-based, with design projects and the university's Formula SAE student team, which has raced at European circuits such as Hockenheim and Barcelona since 2005. Graduates are prepared for roles in automotive design, engineering and production management, and many go on to a master's in a related field.

name: Civil and Environmental Engineering
overview: A newly designed degree that trains engineers to design, manage and maintain civil structures and infrastructure such as bridges, dams, roads, railways and water systems, while adding environmental topics: circular-economy principles for natural resources and energy, and the design and upkeep of plants that treat gaseous, liquid and solid industrial waste. Typical first-year courses in civil engineering include calculus, physics, chemistry and computing, followed by mechanics of structures, hydraulics, geotechnics and construction. Graduates work in engineering firms, public bodies and construction on infrastructure and environmental projects, or continue to a master's.

name: Computer Engineering (entirely in English)
overview: The degree prepares you to manage complex digital systems and to weigh alternative IT solutions, working alongside other engineers and disciplines. Courses are taught by professors who are active in research with Italian and international academic and industrial partners, so theory is tied to examples from practice. Typical first-year subjects in computer engineering include calculus, physics, programming, computer architecture and electronics, followed by algorithms, databases, operating systems, networks and software engineering. Graduates usually go into software, systems and IT roles in companies and public bodies, or continue to a master's in computer engineering or related fields.

name: Electronic and Communications Engineering
overview: The degree is multidisciplinary, joining communications, electronics and computer science. Year one covers mathematics, physics, computer science, computer networks and electronics; year two continues with advanced mathematics and physics and the basics of electronic systems; year three turns to ICT topics: algorithms and programming, digital transmission and computer networks, and advanced electronic systems. Teaching is in English, chosen as the working language of ICT. Graduates are prepared for careers in information and communications technology, and typically continue to a master's in electronic, communications or computer engineering.

name: Mechanical Engineering (entirely in English)
overview: The degree gives a broad technical and scientific base in industrial engineering and then adds mechanical specialisation, with applications in design, production, management, automation and aerospace. Learning combines lectures with laboratory work and hands-on projects, student teams that work on real engineering projects, an industrial internship and a thesis. Mobility options include a special exchange with China (PoliTong), a partnership programme with the USA and a wide European and worldwide partner network. Graduates are prepared to manage industrial transformation and innovation, working in industry or continuing to a master's and PhD research.

name: Applied Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence
overview: You build a general base in programming languages, software design and development, algorithms and computational complexity, and discrete structures, then add technical depth in parallel and distributed software, computer architecture, networks, databases, human-computer interaction, artificial intelligence and information security. Machine learning, deep learning and learning from big data run through the later courses, and an internship and a thesis are part of the path. Graduates can take junior roles building computing solutions on their own, mostly in software companies and IT consulting firms, especially in big data analytics, or continue to a master's in computer science or a related field.

name: Bioinformatics
overview: The degree joins biology and computer science or information engineering. From the first year you take mathematics, physics, statistics and chemistry alongside the structure and function of living systems at molecular and cellular level, then genetics, biochemistry, cell and molecular biology, programming and the design of software systems, with plenty of credits given to lab work. Internships in companies, public bodies and laboratories and study periods at other universities are part of the design. Graduates work as technical staff, researchers or analysts in biomedical research, health services and biotech or pharmaceutical firms, running systems for clinical and bioinformatic data, or continue to specialised study.

name: Business Sciences
overview: The degree builds a multidisciplinary base in business economics, finance, law and mathematics and statistics, so that you can understand how public and private organisations, real and financial markets and their economic, institutional and environmental setting work. Particular attention goes to reading company data critically, understanding decision processes and judging economic and financial performance, including questions of sustainability. Graduates work as junior to mid-level consultants and staff in budgeting, financial planning, auditing, management control, corporate taxation and strategy, in companies, auditing firms, consultancies and public administration.

name: Economics and Finance
overview: The core courses cover economics and applied economics, public finance and economic history, business, mathematics and statistics, and law, so that you can analyse how economic systems and financial markets work with theoretical and empirical tools. Econometrics and statistics build the skills to model economic and financial phenomena and to judge public policy, with attention to growth, development, governance and regulation. Teaching includes seminars, labs and internships, and elective exams let you shape your own path. Graduates work as international economic analysts in international organisations, companies, research centres, public administration and the non-profit sector.

name: Classics
overview: Designed for international students who may have little or no formal background in Classics, the course gives intensive training in Greek and Latin, aiming to take you to the point where you can read complex literary texts. Alongside the languages and literatures you study ancient history, classical archaeology and the legacy of the classical world in medieval, modern and contemporary cultures, with cultural, anthropological and reception perspectives. Field trips, museum visits and library workshops make use of the city of Rome. Graduates work in publishing, journalism and cultural heritage, in spreading knowledge of the ancient world and in translating texts, and many continue to further study.

name: Global Humanities
overview: The degree combines literary, artistic, socio-anthropological, historical-religious and political-legal perspectives within a global and transcultural view. You study migration, interethnic communication and transcultural mediation in relation to diasporas, with history, art history, the history of religions, anthropology, sociology, global and public health and comparative law. From the third year you gain experience through an internship, with placements arranged with partner institutions. Graduates work as cultural mediators in the social sector, in international cooperation and reception organisations, and in public and private institutions dealing with migration, or continue their studies in Italy or abroad.

name: Molecular Biology, Medicinal Chemistry and Computer Science for Pharmaceutical Applications
overview: You build a base in three areas: molecular biology, medicinal chemistry and computer science. Courses cover molecular biology, biomedicine, genetics, pathology and immunology, medicinal chemistry and pharmaceutical technology, together with programming, algorithms for molecular biology and drug chemistry, and mathematical, physical and statistical methods. The aim is to understand how active compounds are found and how information technology is changing that work. Graduates are prepared for basic and applied research in university and industry labs, biotechnology firms, and scientific publishing and communication, or for further study.

name: Sustainable Building Engineering
overview: The degree trains building engineers who weigh the economic, social and environmental effects of changing the built territory. Alongside foundation subjects you take core building engineering courses integrated with traditional civil engineering, with environmental engineering subjects giving weight to sustainability, and you learn to survey and analyse existing buildings and to work with low-impact techniques and materials. The aim is to understand the links between management, design, construction and production at different scales of the building sector. Graduates are intermediate-level professionals who contribute to planning, designing and carrying out interventions to build, transform and conserve buildings.

name: Nursing (Azienda Ospedaliera Sant'Andrea)
overview: The course trains nurses to manage preventive and care interventions for individuals, families and communities, and to look after patients from children to older adults with respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, renal, digestive, neurological, cancer, infectious and orthopaedic problems, as well as perioperative care, safe medication and psychological distress. Theory in basic, clinical and nursing sciences, ethics, law and communication is combined with supervised clinical training at Rome's Sant'Andrea hospital. Graduates are prepared to work as nurses in hospitals and the wider health service, working in teams with other professionals and using the methods of nursing research.

name: Medicine and Surgery "F"
overview: Over six years you move from the basic sciences, typically anatomy, physiology, biochemistry and pathology, to clinical medicine, learning to give safe, high-quality care, to make clinical decisions on prevention, diagnosis and treatment, and to base them on evidence while knowing the limits of your competence. The programme follows international standards in medical education and includes a practical-evaluative internship that is required before registration as a physician. Graduates practise in the national health service and in private or affiliated facilities, working in teams with other health professionals, and can continue to specialist training.

name: Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics
overview: Over six years taught in English, you learn to treat diseases of the mouth and teeth and to restore or maintain oral function, starting from the basic medical sciences and moving into clinical dentistry. A large share of the course is professional training: small-group practical activity guided by teachers within the teaching hospital and in the wider area. Dentists diagnose and treat diseases and anomalies of the teeth, mouth, jaws and related tissues and handle prevention and rehabilitation, and they coordinate dental teams that include hygienists, assistants and dental technicians. Graduates can go on to dental specialty schools such as oral surgery and paediatric dentistry.

name: Building Construction Engineering
overview: The degree trains engineers who design, manage and oversee the production and use of buildings and infrastructure, with the technical and scientific skills of a construction engineer. Typical courses in this field include mathematics and physics, building technology, structures, materials and construction management, and teaching takes place in laboratories with modern equipment. The programme is taught entirely in English on the Ravenna campus and includes Erasmus and overseas exchange options. Graduates work as building designers and technicians who can also coordinate projects and teams as project managers, or continue to a master's degree or a first-level professional master's.

name: Business and Economics
overview: The guiding thread is strategic management, backed by the main business functions, with a focus on how companies grow in international markets. You learn to analyse consumer behaviour in consumer and industrial markets, the theory and techniques of competition and sector analysis, and financial, product and service markets, so that you can work in any business area and cooperate with the others. Data and analytics are used to build sustainable strategies, and double and multiple degrees are available. Graduates move into international managerial roles in consulting, business, non-profit, manufacturing and service companies, or continue to English-taught master's degrees in the School of Economics.

name: Economics and Finance
overview: The first two years cover the basics of economics, and the third year turns to economics and finance, with specific sub-fields of economics, econometrics and finance courses. In the second and third years you can choose elective courses in economics, economic history, business, law, statistics and mathematics. Graduates are prepared to work as junior economic and financial analysts, giving advice to private and public bodies on investment and funding plans, evaluating securities and assessing financial risk, or to move on to economic journalism or to master's studies in economics, finance and management. Labs, internships and fieldwork grants are available.

name: Economics of Tourism and Cities
overview: The first year gives a basis in mathematics, private law, political economy, economic history and geography, and business economics. The later years specialise in the legal governance of territory and tourism, statistics and mathematics for market research, economic models of tourism and cultural industries, urban, regional and transport economics, and marketing, financial analysis and corporate strategy, with digital skills for collecting data and communicating with tourists. Teaching includes labs, internships and a thesis. Graduates work as tourism and city development consultants, destination managers, tourism planners, hotel and hospitality managers, event organisers and economists in the public and private sector.

name: Economics, Politics and Social Sciences
overview: A newer degree that trains you in the social sciences from both quantitative and qualitative angles, combining core teaching in economics and political science with statistics, management and law. You gain the quantitative skills for empirical analysis and the interpretive tools to understand complex economic, political and social settings, nationally and internationally, and the structure is tuned to the needs of the private sector and public administration. Statistics, programming and data analysis are in demand on the job market. Graduates work in international organisations, research centres, NGOs, internationally active companies, demographic institutes and news agencies, in roles such as policy and public-administration management.

name: Genomics
overview: The degree applies computing, mathematics and statistics to genomic data. You start with mathematical analysis, algebra, physics and chemistry, then study genetics, biochemistry and the molecular biology of prokaryotes and eukaryotes, together with programming, statistics, algorithms, multi-scale modelling and computational simulation. Bioinformatics skills include analysing nucleic acids, proteins and omic datasets, mining and managing biological databases and the bioethics of sensitive data, complemented by a data science subject. Learning includes laboratory work, projects, internships and a thesis. Graduates can annotate and curate biological datasets and interpret omic data in systems biology, or continue to further study.

name: International Studies
overview: The course gives a multidisciplinary training that is both theoretical and empirical, always with a comparative and international perspective. Economic, historical, legal and political analysis are used to understand the international system, with subjects such as comparative legal systems, international law and political science, plus two languages, and practical activities let you apply what you learn. You can take internships in international organisations and join exchange programmes, including Erasmus+ study and traineeship periods. Graduates are prepared for international roles and may continue to a second-cycle degree or a first-level professional master's.

name: Management and Economics
overview: The programme centres on management and economics and adds foundations in law, mathematics and statistics seen from an international angle, together with Business English and Cross-Cultural Management. You study business and company law, accounting and financial statements under international standards, business strategy, how the financial system works, consumer behaviour, and microeconomic and macroeconomic theory, and you build data analysis skills. Exchanges for study and internships are available, and you can spend the last semester at the University of Bologna's campus in Buenos Aires. Double degrees exist, and the degree gives access to master's programmes.

name: Pharmacy
overview: The five years move from chemistry, biology, anatomy and human physiology towards medicinal chemistry, pharmacology, toxicology and pharmaceutical technology, with added courses in bioethics, first aid, digital health and pharmaceutical and clinical care. The aim is to train pharmacists who can advise patients on medicines and health products such as cosmetics, food supplements and medical devices, take part in public health campaigns and act as a link between patient, doctor and health service. Internships and dissertation research abroad are possible. Graduates qualify as pharmacists after the state exam, or continue to specialisation schools, doctorates or second-level master's programmes.

name: Medicine and Surgery
overview: Over six years taught in English, you move from the basic medical sciences, typically anatomy, physiology and biochemistry, to clinical medicine and practical training. The programme takes an international view, with attention to health promotion, preventive care, family health and global health, and an orientation that widens options for specialty training and research abroad. Graduates work as physicians in public and private clinics, hospitals and specialised medical centres, hospices, universities and research centres, and national and international health and humanitarian organisations, or go on to further education.

name: Veterinary Medicine
overview: The programme integrates the veterinary subjects across the curriculum, with strong attention to One Health and Circular Health, and builds transversal and soft skills alongside clinical ones. Hands-on training takes place in laboratories, a clinical skills lab, the teaching hospital, a farm and external facilities, and in the final year you tailor your studies through electives and practical training. Teaching in English supports mobility through Erasmus, internships and dissertation work abroad. Veterinarians protect the health of animals, people and the environment, working in clinical care of pets and farm animals, in public health bodies, in research and in food production, or continue to postgraduate study.

name: International Politics, Law and Economics (IPLE)
overview: The shared years cover logic and critical thinking, contemporary history, the history of political theories, public law, comparative social systems, political science, microeconomics and data analysis, then international law, international relations, international macroeconomics, statistics and writing skills. Two curricula run from the first year: International Politics and Economics, which compares politics and economic policy, and International Politics and Law, which adds international and European law. Workshops and internships are on offer. Graduates are prepared for public administration, diplomatic missions, international organisations, NGOs, think tanks and companies in international trade and finance.

name: Medicine and Surgery – International Medical School
overview: The six-year English-taught curriculum joins basic science and clinical activity, organised in integrated teaching blocks from the first year. Learning is by problem-based methods in small groups and discussion of clinical cases, with visiting professors from European and North American universities and exchange programmes with foreign universities. You get early experience in research laboratories, following a translational, bench-to-bedside approach. The degree qualifies you to practise as a physician after a positive evaluation in the training internship and registration, and it is the route into residency programmes and specialty schools, in a range of clinical, healthcare and biomedical roles.

name: Animal Care
overview: The degree centres on the care of animals and their welfare, looking at the individual animal as well as themes that run across species, alongside scientific research and the conservation of terrestrial and aquatic environments. Typical courses in such a degree include biology, anatomy and physiology, animal behaviour, nutrition and welfare. Learning is practical, with field visits to zoos, rehabilitation centres and research facilities and internships that can be done abroad. Graduates work in animal protection and monitoring and in coordinating care alongside veterinarians, biologists and zoologists, and the international outlook supports study for a master's outside Italy.

name: Biology of Human and Environmental Health
overview: You study the biological processes that keep the human body working, how changes in them lead to disease, and how people and their environment affect one another, including the effects of human activity and global environmental change on health. Typical early courses in a biology degree include chemistry, genetics, cell biology, physiology and statistics, and advanced research methods are woven through the programme. The first two years are in Padua, then you take a Human Health path in Padua or an Environmental Health path in Bologna. Graduates go on to master's study in the biological and biomedical sciences.

name: Earth and Climate Dynamics
overview: The degree gives advanced training in Earth science with modern techniques: remote sensing, satellite data processing, geographic information systems, drone technology and basic modelling, applied to climate change. Classroom teaching is combined with practical activities, and typical courses in an Earth science degree include geology, geophysics, mineralogy, oceanography and atmospheric science, with fieldwork. The aim is to build professional skills for working on the complex phenomena of climate change. Graduates usually go into environmental and geoscience consulting, monitoring and public bodies, or on to a master's degree.

name: Economics, Governance and Decision-Making
overview: A transdisciplinary social science degree with a strong methodological stamp, paying attention to ethics and logical reasoning. The first two years are common, covering typical subjects such as economics, politics, philosophy, law, statistics and mathematics, and in the third year you orient yourself towards one of three specialised tracks. Graduates are prepared for junior and consulting positions in public and private organisations, NGOs and international organisations, or for a wide range of master's programmes in Italy and abroad.

name: Information Engineering
overview: The degree gives a broad base in the main areas of information engineering, which are automation, electronics, computer science and telecommunications, resting on physics and mathematics. A strong methodological approach to analysing problems runs through the courses, which are taught in a blended format. Typical subjects include calculus, programming, signals and systems, control and electronic circuits. Graduates develop critical analysis, design and problem-solving skills and can work in private companies, public administration or independent practice, in Italy or abroad, or continue to a master's degree in engineering.

name: Psychological Science
overview: The course covers the main sectors of psychology, general, social and psychodynamic, together with the methods of scientific investigation, and gives theory and experimental and clinical work equal weight through seminars and workshops. Typical courses include general, developmental and social psychology, psychometrics, statistics and research methods. An international dimension comes from a network of partnerships with training institutions. Graduates work in psychometric and psychosocial assessment, education, human resources, business and third-sector organisations, or continue to a master's degree in psychology.

name: Techniques and Methods in Psychological Science
overview: Delivered entirely by distance learning, the degree teaches the foundations of the main fields of psychology, the methods of scientific research, and cognitive and emotional processes together with their psychobiological bases. Typical courses include general and developmental psychology, statistics and research methods. It trains you to design intervention projects for communities, in emergencies and to improve well-being, at national and international level. Graduates work in psychological well-being services, research, training and organisational development, continuing education, and organisations dealing with migration, inclusion and human rights, or continue to a master's degree.

name: Medicine and Surgery
overview: Taught in English in Venice over six years, the course takes a holistic view of the person, with attention to health promotion, preventive medicine and global health. Learning follows integrated pathways with active student involvement, and a clinical approach begins in the first year, to prepare doctors for multicultural healthcare settings. Typical early subjects in a medical degree include anatomy, physiology and biochemistry. Graduates can enter specialist training programmes in Italy and practise in public or private healthcare facilities, independently or in teams.

name: Comparative, European and International Legal Studies (CEILS)
overview: The degree rests on four foundations: comparative legal systems, European law, the historical and philosophical bases of modern legal thought, and substantive and procedural law in both private and public areas, always viewed through comparative, European and international lenses. Its distinctive feature is a comparative, international and transnational approach to law, preparing you to work across legal contexts. Alongside law you improve your English and study a second European language, German, French, Spanish or Italian. You can apply for internships in international institutions. Graduates are prepared for roles needing knowledge of several legal systems, especially in international organisations and EU settings.

name: Computer Science (English track)
overview: The first two years give you the basics: mathematics, programming and algorithms, and systems and information management, with software design and development. From the second year you add electives matched to your interests. Computer science is treated as a discipline between science and engineering, using scientific inquiry and rigorous engineering methods, and the degree is recognised by the Italian computer science professors' association and the national computing association. Typical early courses include calculus, discrete mathematics, programming, computer architecture, databases and operating systems. Graduates are prepared to design and develop software as an industry activity.

name: Computer, Communications and Electronic Engineering (English track)
overview: The first year builds foundations in mathematical analysis, physics, programming, geometry and linear algebra, and after that you take transversal courses in three areas of specialisation: computer engineering, communications and electronics. Work is project-based, in laboratories using design equipment and software. Typical later courses include digital systems, signals, networks, electronic circuits and software engineering. Graduates usually work in information and communication technology and electronics companies or continue to a master's degree in engineering.

name: Business & Management
overview: You cover the main functional areas of business, accounting and finance, marketing, strategy, economics and organisational behaviour, together with the economic, social, political and legal environment in which firms decide. Courses run on a block system: you focus on one subject for two to six weeks and take the exam straight after, which lets international and visiting faculty and business professionals teach. Cohorts are small, with case studies, seminars, workshops, group presentations and business games. After three years you can add a fourth year in the US at Kent State or Southern Illinois University Edwardsville for an American BSc. Internship and Erasmus options are available.

name: Economics and Finance with Data Science
overview: Economics and finance are combined with data science and its applications. The first two years give foundations in economics, and in the third year you specialise in economics, finance or statistics. Alongside lectures there are lab activities such as data analysis labs, and the final thesis may be based on research in a company or research institution. The degree works with the Collegio Carlo Alberto, the UNITA university network and universities in Europe and beyond. Graduates work as economists, policy experts and analysts in banking, insurance, consultancy, government agencies and international companies, or continue to master's degrees in economics, finance, statistics, actuarial science or management.

name: Global Law and Transnational Legal Studies
overview: The first year gives basic knowledge of the main legal fields from a global viewpoint. In the second year you deepen European and global law through comparison and study the main European and international institutions, and the third year looks at legal practice and decision-making in European and international courts, with electives to specialise. Teaching combines presentations, tutorials, seminars, simulations of legal process and traineeships, and you are encouraged to train abroad through Erasmus+, traineeships and scholarships. Graduates work in the legal divisions of multinational organisations, in institutions and in NGOs and the third sector.

name: Medicine and Surgery (MedInTO)
overview: The six-year programme is built around courses for each year plus elective learning activities, with a degree thesis at the end. Clinical training in clerkships is central, supported by a centre for advanced medical simulation and an e-learning platform, and typical early subjects include anatomy, physiology and biochemistry. Graduates are prepared to practise in national and international settings, to start specialist training in any branch of medicine and surgery, and to apply evidence-based medicine ethically. A MD-PhD programme opens from the second year for qualified students, and Erasmus and international mobility, including research placements abroad, are available.
